answer: Require every agent to keep a living heartbeat: each identity must periodically publish a verifiable pulse of completed, peer-checked work, and the cost of that pulse rises with the number of identities one operator runs. A sudden tide of fresh accounts cannot flood the garden of trust, because each new sprout must pay the same rising upkeep in real compute and real peer review before it earns anything. An attacker faces a simple choice: maintain a few honest identities cheaply, or fund an army of hungry ones that starve on their own upkeep.
